Key takeaways about scholarships for teachers

  • Scholarships for teachers include awards for undergraduates, graduate students, and career changers.
  • These awards are free money for school which can help you focus on training, borrow less, and access more opportunities.
  • Many scholarships are available specifically for teachers in high-need subjects or locations.
  • You can strengthen your application by highlighting your experience and commitment to the field
  • Scholly Scholarships can help you find scholarships related to your teaching interest, and you can apply our $2,000 No Essay Scholarship every month.

Whether you’re earning your first teaching credential, pursuing a master’s in education, or switching careers to make a difference in the classroom, scholarships can lower your costs by a lot. This guide highlights top scholarships for teachers, explains eligibility and application tips, and connects you to resources to help you discover more funding.

What are teaching scholarships?

Teaching scholarships are awards that provide free money you don’t have to repay to support education majors, licensed teachers, paraprofessionals, and future educators. They may be offered by schools of education, professional associations, nonprofits, or state programs, and can cover tuition, books, fees, or professional development. Many are merit-based, need-based, or targeted to high-need subjects (like STEM or special education) and high-need locations (like rural or Title I districts).

Why scholarships matter for teachers

Education programs often require clinical placements and licensure exams, adding time and costs. Scholarships help you focus on training, reduce debt, and expand opportunities—from student teaching abroad to pursuing endorsements (e.g. ESL, reading specialist, special education) that improve job prospects and impact.

How to qualify for teaching scholarships

While requirements vary, you’ll typically strengthen your application by:

  • Meeting academic criteria, including a minimum GPA or prerequisite courses.
  • Declaring an eligible major, usually education, early childhood education, special education, or a secondary content area.
  • Documenting service or commitment, such as tutoring, volunteering, or agreeing to teach in high need subjects/locations.
  • Submitting a strong personal statement that shows your classroom impact and future goals.
  • Completing required forms (some awards may request FAFSA® information to verify need.

Pro tip: Keep a simple portfolio including your resume, unofficial transcript, licensure plan, fieldwork log, and references to reuse across applications.

Top scholarships for teachers

  1. $2,000 No Essay Scholarship (Monthly) – A quick apply award that takes minutes to enter. Ideal for education majors, graduate students in teaching, and eligible adult learners.
  2. Future educator scholarships – Awards for undergraduates in teacher prep programs; often merit-based with service components.
  3. Graduate scholarships for teachers – Funding for licensed teachers pursuing M.Ed., MAT, or Ed.S. degrees; some target literacy, SPED, or instructional technology.
  4. Subject-area teaching scholarships – Support for math, science, bilingual/ESL, CTE, and special education—fields where districts need qualified educators most.
  5. Regional and state teaching scholarships – Local foundations and state programs offering awards to residents or those committing to teach instate.
  6. Professional Association awards – Grants and scholarships from education organizations for classroom projects, certification, and continuing education.

Looking for more? Use Scholly Scholarships to find teaching scholarships by subject, degree level, and state.

How to apply

  1. Build your scholarship timeline: Track monthly deadlines and align with academic terms, test dates, and student teaching.
  2. Prepare core materials: Resume, transcript, recommendation letters, licensure plan, and a universal personal statement tailored to each scholarship opportunity.
  3. Use tools like Scholly Scholarships to find top scholarships for teachers by major, state, and background; then filter for high-need subjects and renewable awards.
  4. Apply early and often: Small awards add up—and many are renewable.

Additional resources for teachers

Whether you’re preparing for student teaching, earning your teaching credential, or advancing your career with a graduate degree, these curated resources can help you find scholarships tailored to your goals, interests, background, and teaching pathways.

  • Scholarships by major
    If you're specializing in early childhood education, elementary education, secondary subjects (like math, science, English, or history), or special education, this directory helps you quickly find awards designed for your exact teaching path. Many teaching focused scholarships prioritize majors linked to teacher shortages, so browsing by academic area can increase your chances.
  • Scholarships for high school seniors
    A great starting point for future educators still in high school. Many teacher prep programs offer “early commitment” scholarships, and applying during senior year helps you enter your education major with funding already secured. These awards are perfect for students planning to major in education, child development, psychology, or subject area teaching fields.
  • Scholarships for college students
    Already in an education program? You can still apply for teaching scholarships during freshman through senior years. This page highlights awards that support student teachers, education majors completing practicum hours, and upper division coursework like curriculum design or classroom management.
  • Scholarships for first-generation students
    If you’re the first in your family to pursue college—or teacher certification—these scholarships help reduce financial barriers during a demanding degree path that includes coursework, field placements, and exam prep. This is especially helpful for future educators balancing school with work or family commitments.
  • Scholarships for adults
    Many adults pursue teaching as a second career, especially in high-need subjects. This resource is ideal for paraprofessionals, substitute teachers, instructional aides, or career changers entering teacher prep programs later in life. These scholarships often support flexible or accelerated credential pathways.
  • Scholarships for women
    Women make up a large percentage of the teaching workforce, and many programs offer support for both undergraduate and graduate degrees in the education field. You'll also find awards for women in underrepresented teaching subject areas—such as STEM—as well as scholarships specifically for Black women educators.
  • LGBTQ+ scholarships
    Educators who identify as LGBTQ+ can find financial support and community focused scholarships that celebrate diversity and leadership in education. Many awards also value applicants committed to creating inclusive classrooms and supporting LGBTQ+ youth.
  • Scholarships by state
    Teacher shortages vary from state to state, and many states offer generous funding—sometimes including tuition assistance in exchange for teaching commitments in local schools. These state opportunities often have fewer applicants and higher award amounts, making them especially valuable for future and current teachers.

Pursuing a career in education is both inspiring and demanding—and the right scholarships can make your path more affordable and accessible. By exploring the resources above, staying organized in your search, and applying consistently, you can unlock funding that helps you focus on what matters most: developing your skills, shaping young minds, and making a meaningful impact in your community.

Frequently asked questions about scholarships for teachers

What are scholarships for teachers?

They’re awards that help current and future educators pay for degrees, credentials, or ongoing development—no repayment required.

Who qualifies for teaching scholarships?

Education majors, licensed teachers pursuing advanced study, paraprofessionals advancing credentials, and career changers entering teacher prep programs typically qualify. Criteria vary by award.

Are teaching scholarships renewable?

Many are—especially those tied to multi‑year programs or service commitments. Check each award’s renewal rules.

What scholarships are available for teachers?

From general education awards to subject area and state specific programs, you’ll find options at the college, association, nonprofit, and foundation levels—plus the $2,000 No Essay Scholarship by Sallie.

Do I need to complete FAFSA® to apply?

Some need-based‑ teaching scholarships request FAFSA® to verify financial need; merit-‑based awards may not. Always review eligibility.

Are there scholarships for teachers in high need subjects or locations?

Yes—many awards prioritize areas like math, science, bilingual education, and special education, or districts with high staffing needs. 

Are small scholarships worth it?

Absolutely. Smaller awards stack and can cover books, fees, exam costs, and classroom supplies—every dollar reduces your out-of-pocket.

Need more money for college?

Private student loans can help you cover additional eligible school-certified expenses.
